coop report. All six families are done. No real server apply was run for any of them; every apply is tested only against the fake guest. `tsc --noEmit` shows 0 errors. The 6 new `test/cfg-*.test.ts` files pass, and so do the 25 existing test files that touch game-config, game-variant or game-control (368 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped).

**Branch:** `feature/game-config-coop`, worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-cfg-coop`, from `feature/game-config-apply-core` (60aa1cdd07). Nothing is merged or pushed.
**Commits:**
- 064388101c: appliers, specs, schema fixes, `game-variant` bake.
- b75f8b1c83: tests and docs.

**Notes:** `/root/agent-notes/cfg-coop.md`

## Per family (truth read from each image's own scripts on GitHub)

**satisfactory** (wolveix image): all five fields are `recreate`.
- Fields: maxPlayers, autosaveNum, maxTickRate, disableSeasonalEvents, maxObjects.
- Mechanism: `run.sh` turns the env vars MAXPLAYERS, AUTOSAVENUM, MAXTICKRATE, DISABLESEASONALEVENTS and MAXOBJECTS into `-ini:` launch args on every start. We rebuild the container with the new env. The ini files are not edited, because `run.sh` overrides them on every start.
- Defaults (seasonal off, default max objects) are left unset, so they cause no rebuild.
- The schema had no `envKey`, so checkout values were never baked at install. They are now, and I corrected the false "doesn't reach the server" help text.
- Satisfactory ServerSettings and the Satisfactory API are not in the schema, so nothing there.

**factorio**: all fields are `restart`.
- Fields: name, description, max_players, game_password, allow_commands, autosave_interval, autosave_slots, non_blocking_saving, afk_autokick_interval, visibility, admins.
- Mechanism: top-level keys of `/opt/factorio/config/server-settings.json`. The image never maps env to settings. `admins` is written whole to `server-adminlist.json`, so `/promote` entries made in-game are replaced when the field is saved.
- `visibility` is only turned on if `username` and `token`/`password` already exist in the file. Otherwise it is left alone and the customer is told why. Turning it off is always written.
- Fresh installs now build `server-settings.json` from the game's own example, read out of the image and patched in python3. Any failure falls back to the image's own seeding.
- Map-gen settings are not in the schema, so none.
- RCON `/config set` was not used.

**abioticfactor**: all four fields are `recreate`.
- Fields: SteamServerName, MaxServerPlayers, ServerPassword, WorldSaveName.
- Mechanism: env vars go onto the game command line on every start.
- The image has `${ServerPassword:-password}`, so a blank password silently becomes "password". "Blank = open server" was false. Help text and applier note now say so.
- The image expands the password unquoted, so a password with whitespace or `* ? [ ] \` is held back. The other fields still apply and the result is `ok: false`.
- WorldSaveName selects or creates a save. The old save is kept.

**corekeeper**: all five fields are `recreate`.
- Fields: worldName, maxPlayers, gameId, password, worldMode.
- Mechanism: WORLD_NAME, MAX_PLAYERS, GAME_ID, PASSWORD and WORLD_MODE become launch args on every start.
- Schema `envKey`s were missing, so checkout values were never baked. Fixed.
- A password over 28 characters, or a gameId that isn't 15-28 letters/digits, is held back with a note.
- Not confirmed: whether the game applies worldName and worldMode to an already-created world. They are still marked `recreate`, with an honest "existing world may keep its own" note.

**necesse**: all five fields are `recreate`.
- Fields: WORLD_NAME, SERVER_SLOTS, SERVER_PASSWORD, SERVER_OWNER, SERVER_MOTD.
- Mechanism: env becomes quoted `-world -slots -password -owner -motd` args. An empty value omits the arg, so a blank password really is open.
- SERVER_OWNER and SERVER_MOTD are baked when set, because the catalog script doesn't declare them.
- I read the source of the repo that matches the Docker Hub description, but did not confirm the `:latest` tag is built from that exact entrypoint.

**barotrauma**: all seven fields are `recreate`.
- SERVERNAME, PASSWORD, MAX_PLAYERS and PUBLICITY are patched into `/opt/barotrauma/config/serversettings.xml`, the root attributes `name`, `password`, `MaxPlayers`, `IsPublic`.
- The image reads its env only while creating the config on first boot, and its `sed` is case-sensitive. MAX_PLAYERS and PUBLICITY therefore never reached the file, even at install. The applier fixes this for existing servers, and the auto-queued job fixes fresh non-default orders.
- The game may rewrite the files while running, so the sequence is stop, patch, start, read back. If the start fails, the files and container are restored.
- After the start, the password is only checked as set-versus-blank, in case the game hashes it. If the game drops a value while starting, the result is `ok: false` with a note.
- OWNER_STEAMNAME and OWNER_STEAMID add or update a `<Client name steamid permissions="All">` in `clientpermissions.xml`. Other clients are never removed, and an earlier owner stays in the file. The `steamid` attribute shape comes from the image's own template and is unconfirmed on a current game build.
- INSTALL_LUA is a normal env-recreate. Turning it off does not uninstall the Lua/C# files.
- Even the baseline is unverified: Barotrauma could not be provisioned at all in the 2026-09 mods wave (steamcmd "Missing configuration").

## Decisions and flags for the owner
- **Abiotic Factor:** the image cannot run an open server (blank password becomes "password"). The options are to require a password at checkout or to accept the help-text correction I made. Changing checkout is outside my brief.
- **Factorio public listing** needs a factorio.com username and token in the server's settings file. Nothing sets them for customers.
- **Barotrauma:** consider a live provision test before trusting any of it.

- `lib/game-config-appliers.ts`: 6 imports and 6 `APPLIER_SPECS` lines.
- `worker/game-config-appliers/index.ts`: 6 imports and 6 `register()` lines.
- `worker/game-variant.ts`: 1 import, plus a delimited `BEGIN/END cfg-coop` block of 3 lines. I changed the `wrapDockerGameService(...)` argument from `scriptWithFivem` to `scriptWithCoop`, so expect a trivial conflict if other agents edit that same line.

  - `envKey`s added to satisfactory and corekeeper.
  - Help text corrected for satisfactory, factorio visibility, abiotic ServerPassword/WorldSaveName and corekeeper password.
  - The satisfactory, corekeeper and abiotic edits are behavioural: envKeys change what checkout bakes, and the abiotic help text is now accurate.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`: 10 rows inserted before the `(next family)` row, plus an appended "Co-op wave facts" subsection at end of file.
- `kit/*` and `test/_fake-docker-guest.ts` are untouched. No `kit/rcon` was needed.

## New files
- `lib/game-applier-specs/{satisfactory,factorio,abioticfactor,corekeeper,necesse,barotrauma,env-fields,coop-setup}.ts`
- `worker/game-config-appliers/{satisfactory,factorio,abioticfactor,corekeeper,necesse,barotrauma,env-fields}.ts`
- `test/_cfg-coop.ts`
- `test/cfg-{satisfactory,factorio,abioticfactor,corekeeper,necesse,barotrauma}.test.ts`

## Not verified
- No real container, game, or Steam/Factorio/Barotrauma process was touched by any apply path.
- The Factorio fresh-install seed was run for real with python3 against an example-shaped file. The `docker run --rm --entrypoint cat` step is not exercised.
- Barotrauma's game-side file rewriting is unconfirmed (see above).
- The Core Keeper name and mode semantics are unconfirmed (see above).

All six families are built on `feature/game-config-coop`, but none was applied to a real server — tests use the fake guest only. `tsc --noEmit` shows 0 errors and the full test run shows 0 failures. The brief asked me to say this for every family.

**What each family does** (all read off the images' own scripts and docs):

| Family | Fields | Mechanism | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| satisfactory | maxPlayers, autosaveNum, maxTickRate, disableSeasonalEvents, maxObjects | env vars that the image turns into `-ini:` launch args on every start | recreate |
| factorio | name, description, max_players, game_password, allow_commands, autosave interval/slots, non_blocking_saving, afk_autokick_interval, visibility, admins | keys in `server-settings.json`; admins written whole to `server-adminlist.json` | restart |
| abioticfactor | SteamServerName, MaxServerPlayers, ServerPassword, WorldSaveName | env vars on the game command line | recreate |
| corekeeper | worldName, maxPlayers, gameId, password, worldMode | env vars that become launch args | recreate |
| necesse | WORLD_NAME, SERVER_SLOTS, SERVER_PASSWORD, SERVER_OWNER, SERVER_MOTD | env vars that become quoted launch args | recreate |
| barotrauma | SERVERNAME, PASSWORD, MAX_PLAYERS, PUBLICITY, owner name and SteamID, INSTALL_LUA | settings and permissions XML patched with the game stopped, then restarted and read back; INSTALL_LUA is an env rebuild | recreate |

**Findings worth knowing:**
- **Satisfactory and Core Keeper:** checkout values were never baked at install because the schema fields had no `envKey`. They are now, and I corrected the misleading help text.
- **Abiotic Factor:** the image turns a blank password into the literal "password", so "Blank = open server" was false. I fixed the help text and the applier says so. A password with whitespace or `* ? [ ] \` breaks the launch, so it is held back while the other fields still apply.
- **Barotrauma:** the image reads its env only when it first creates the config, and its `sed` never matched `MaxPlayers` or `IsPublic`. Those two never reached the file even at install. The applier fixes this for existing servers.
- **Factorio:** public listing is only turned on if factorio.com credentials are already in the settings file. Otherwise it is left off and the customer is told why.

**Not confirmed:**
- Whether Core Keeper applies world name and world mode to an existing world is undocumented, so those two fields carry a note rather than a promise.
- I did not confirm the Necesse `:latest` image is built from the entrypoint I read.
- Barotrauma's owner-entry format comes from the image's own template, and its game-side file rewriting is unconfirmed. It also failed to provision at all in the 2026-09 mods wave.

**Owner decisions needed:**
- **Abiotic Factor blank password:** the image can't run an open server. Either require a password at checkout, or accept the help-text correction I made. Changing checkout was outside my brief.
- **Factorio public listing:** nothing currently puts customers' factorio.com credentials into the settings file.

**Shared files touched:**
- `lib/game-config-appliers.ts`: 6 imports and 6 spec lines.
- `worker/game-config-appliers/index.ts`: 6 imports and 6 `register()` lines.
- `worker/game-variant.ts`: one import and a delimited 3-line block. It changes one `wrapDockerGameService` argument, so expect a trivial merge conflict if another agent edited that line.
- `lib/game-config.ts`: `envKey`s and help text for my families only.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`: 10 table rows plus an appended subsection.

The kit and the fake guest are untouched. The test files are `test/cfg-*.test.ts`, and notes are in `/root/agent-notes/cfg-coop.md`.
